Updated assessment incorporating SLOOS and FSR:

- Policy stance: Still highly accommodative and consistent with FAIT—policy rate at 0–0.25%, IOER at 0.15% anchoring the funds rate, ongoing Treasury ($80B) and agency MBS ($40B) purchases, and active repo/ON RRP operations—supporting growth and smooth market functioning.

- SLOOS credit supply signal: Net easing across many categories supports the transmission of accommodative policy. Banks eased standards on consumer credit (credit cards, auto, and general consumer) and reduced minimum credit score thresholds; large banks eased for HELOCs and GSE-eligible mortgages; standards eased for investment-grade firms. This indicates improving access to credit for households and higher-quality corporates. Offsets: relative to pre-pandemic levels, standards in some consumer segments remain tighter; foreign banks tightened standards for below-investment-grade firms and kept IG largely unchanged; some policies for C&I lending remain conservative. CRE underwriting remains cautious (nonfarm nonresidential/construction), consistent with lingering pockets of stress.

- FSR context: Financial conditions are easy, but vulnerabilities persist—stretched valuations, elevated business leverage (especially lower-rated), and structural fragilities in short-term funding and open-end funds. Bank capital/liquidity remain strong.

Net: With SLOOS showing a broad easing in bank lending standards, the balance of evidence is more supportive for growth than in the FSR-only view, though tempered by remaining tightness for riskier borrowers and CRE. Tone shifts modestly more positive.

sentiment score = 0.50
